_doc: SecurityInsight Pro -- the template pack the templates SHIPPED with this code are (#250). Template pack versions are their own series, starting at 1.0 -- NOT the code version. Setup and the update hook install these templates as this pack (staged, published, recorded as installed). The vendor raises it only when the shipped templates themselves change; later template versions reach installs as packs 1.1, 1.2, ... through the update ring (setup\New-SITemplatePack.ps1, then setup\Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Kind templates -Ring <n>). A pack version is immutable: the same version never names different content. Fingerprint pins that: it is the template-set fingerprint of exactly the content this version names (Get-SIProShippedPackPin). #405, from pack 1.3 on (ClassificationReviewed true): the pack version names the MICROSOFT CONTENT only (the microsoft-class templates) -- fix and default templates have no version of their own, ride the code version and are installed with the code on every install, also one already on this pack, so a change to them (e.g. #400, 2026-10-07: the empty-key joins in the device / Azure recommendation and sign-in reports) needs NO bump; only a changed Microsoft item does, and SIv3-TemplateDefaultPack then prints the next pack version and the exact Fingerprint to set. Not reviewed (false/absent): Fingerprint is over every shipped template and any template change needs a bump, or an install that already has this version never receives the change. History (1.0 -> 1.1, 2026-10-05: the ordered risk index and two Azure recommendation fixes had shipped under 1.0 and were never applied; 1.1 -> 1.2, 2026-10-05: the default tier rule AssetProfileByDefaultTier; 1.2 -> 1.3, 2026-10-05: the Azure recommendation reports keep a recommendation whose Exposure Graph node is missing and hand off to the Defender report by assessment key as well; Microsoft content 1.3 -> 1.4, 2026-10-07: #401 -- the lateral-movement attack-path reports list each device once (a device found by both the vulnerable-device and the Azure node sets was kept at random); Microsoft content 1.4 -> 1.5, 2026-10-09: #505 -- the attack-path reports read their end assets from the CI (SI_CI_CL) instead of the profile tables; Microsoft content 1.5 -> 1.6, 2026-10-10: the attack-path reports read the joined device / path end / source from their own fed factor sets and show the catalog's factor names; Microsoft content 1.6 -> 1.7, 2026-10-10: the two public IP to VM CVE attack paths read the CVE's last-modified date from either graph property path (a reshaped property no longer drops the age filter silently); Microsoft content 1.7 -> 1.8, 2026-10-10: the attack-path reports follow the risk factor model v2 -- the factor short names and the factor sets they read changed with the catalog; Microsoft content 1.8 -> 1.9, 2026-10-15: #677 round 2 -- the 10 attack-path reports slice on the path's target, and a catalog-wide join guard; Microsoft content 1.9 -> 1.10, 2026-10-15: #690 -- the vulnerable-device-to-Azure attack paths match the graph's subscription label (subscriptions), the credential-based lateral movement compares every label ignoring case (entra-userCookie), takes every credential and Azure target the graph holds and its Detailed report is one row per path with the source's CI id, and an unknown tier stays empty instead of tier 3; Microsoft content 1.10 -> 1.11, 2026-10-15: #690 -- the two public IP to VM CVE attack paths start from the graph's routing nodes labelled IP address as well as the Azure public IP resource, compared ignoring case, follow a network interface to its machine and tie the machine to the graph node of the same name that carries its CVEs; Microsoft content 1.11 -> 1.12, 2026-10-15: #690 (15) -- the public IP to VM CVE attack path's top severity band is Very High (it was "Critical", a value outside the five SI severities that the severity scope dropped); Microsoft content 1.12 -> 1.13, 2026-10-19: rc12 -- the SOC attack-path reports (#691: four new lateral-movement pairs, each Summary pairing its assets with the CI id), one report structure with pinned output names and two findings linked into one (#692 / #693); Microsoft content 1.13 -> 1.14, 2026-10-19: #809 -- the attack-path reports report the resources inside a subscription or resource group, never the scope itself, once per resource; Microsoft content 1.14 -> 1.15, 2026-10-19: #692 -- every report carries the generated data-out block, and the two Defender recommendation reports the bucket filter (one slice per hash of the resource) -- a one-time fingerprint change the owner accepted, carried (data-model\report-fingerprint-carry.locked.json): no finding closes because of it; Microsoft content 1.15 -> 1.16, 2026-10-23: the two managed-identity attack-path reports give a target no CI links the tier of its top-level resource's CI, else its subscription's most critical CI (the joins guarded against an empty key) -- the same rows, the tier filled, carried (report-target-tier-2026-10-23): no finding closes because of it). Packs 1.1 and 1.2 were pre-release, on ring 1 only. 2026-10-07 (lane-pack14): the 1.3 pin was re-scoped from every shipped template to its Microsoft content (the same 12 attack-path reports, fingerprint identical before and after #400) -- 1.3 is not renumbered. #405 (operator decision 2026-10-06): one template pack per release -- 3.0.0 ships this content, and its Microsoft content is the first Microsoft content pack, 1.3. ClassificationReviewed: the classification of every shipped template (config\template-classification.locked.json: fix | default | microsoft) was decided and recorded (docs\template-classification-3.0.0.md); true switches the split install on -- fix and default templates are installed with the code, never held; Microsoft content packs are installed automatically unless the install holds them. false (or absent) keeps the old behaviour: every template change waits for a review on Template releases. A later release whose classification has not been decided ships false.
Name: Default templates 1.16
